text: The slot holds the head `prototypes + sentences` for `tinyclip-39m-16` (species_taxon_com, beta 8, bias for species without photos 0.8), fitted on `images/alachua-2025 (two thirds of val)`, with 5911 species rows, and a bias a row. Every photo's vector (`images/alachua-2025.wasm-int8-per-channel`) went through `tools/fusion/fuse.py`, the reference of the page's arithmetic, with the slot's own files as the page reads them (half-precision rows). Settings: rule `mix`, t_kind 0.5, w_kind 0.7, alpha_prior 1. On 565 tuning photos (the third of val kept for tuning) the thresholds came out as name_at 0.90 and offer_at 0.94. On the 4197 test photos the kind of eye is right for 87.3% (86.3 to 88.3); the top species is right for 36.3% (34.9 to 37.8) and is among the first five for 58.8% (57.3 to 60.2). `person` was said for 0.07% of these photos and `none` for 0.07%; the set holds neither. The top species from fuse.py differs from a direct matrix computation on the same files for 0 photos. The kinds head is `kind rows fitted on the fitting photos and the extra set (a kind's photos weighted by the inverse square root of their number)`. With kind_at 0.50 (set on wildlife tuning photos and the extra set's tuning third), the page asserts a kind for 78.8% (77.6 to 80.1) of the wildlife test photos and is right for 95.5% (94.8 to 96.1) of those; for the 21.2% (19.9 to 22.4) where it is not sure, the true kind is among its three likeliest for 90.4% (88.5 to 92.4). On the 1240 test photos of people, cats, dogs, grazing animals and rooms (`images/coco-kinds.wasm-int8-per-channel`), the kind is right for 98.1% (97.3 to 98.8); the page asserts a kind for 95.5% (94.3 to 96.6) and is right for 99.2% (98.7 to 99.7) of those; where it is not sure the true kind is among its three likeliest for 94.6% (89.3 to 100.0). A species is named on 6.2% (4.9 to 7.7) of these photos. The slot needs: species.bias_url (build 7 of the page); kinds.bias (build 7 of the page); fusion.rule mix (build 7 of the page); fusion.kind_at (the build of the page that has the answer `not sure`).
